The transition to a stage with the high strain-hardening coefficient θIII may be associated with the multiple slip stage.
The main type of slipping dislocations observed in the present work had Burgers vector b = <010>, regardless of temperature and chemical composition.

Thus, a decrease in the yield strength of B2(L2 1)-austenite of Ni 54 Fe 19 Ga 27 and (Ni 54 Fe 19 Ga 27 ) 99.7 B 0.3 alloys with increasing temperature was caused, first, by the thermally activated movement of < 010 > dislocations relevant to B2 alloys.
Second, grain boundary slip cannot be excluded; however, metallographic evidence was not found in the present research.
The absence of significant plastic deformation of γ -phase particles may confirm the dynamic stress recovery and relaxation due to particle growth during high-temperature loading.
